subject: Acme Q2 Dedicated GPU reservation & autoscale exception
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Acme Q2 Dedicated GPU reservation & autoscale exception

Team — looping you in on a high-priority request from Acme AI. They want to reserve dedicated capacity for an upcoming product launch in Q2. Key asks are below and I've attached their reservation PDF and our current inventory snapshot.

Quick summary:
- Customer: Acme AI (Samantha Ho)
- Requested capacity: 40 x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool) from 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30
- Autoscale exception: customer requires that these instances not be subject to normal burst/eviction policies for that window (they will be running steady inference traffic and latency SLOs are critical)
- Commercial: they are open to a 3-month commitment and expect pricing to be inline w/ reserved capacity discounts

Ask from each team:
- Infra (Rishi): feasibility + any constraints on pinning/reserving 40 GPUs and consequences for autoscaling rules
- Product Ops (Stephanie): whether we can approve a temporary autoscale exception and what telemetry/tracking you need
- Finance/Procurement (Laura): what contract/PO steps are required to enable reservation before we lock capacity

Attachments: acme_reservation_request_0302.pdf, gpu_inventory_snapshot_0302.csv

Samantha indicated urgency (launch date in April) — I flagged we need a decision by end of week to secure capacity.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Ho <samantha.ho@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 16:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Q2 Dedicated GPU reservation & autoscale exception

Marissa — thanks for the quick start. Confirming the ask from our side: 40 dedicated GPUs reserved exclusively for Acme between Apr 1 and Jun 30.

We cannot tolerate preemption during our peak windows (08:00-20:00 PT) and need a firm SLA on latency (p50 < 60ms for our requested batch sizes). We can sign a 3-month SOW + PO immediately if Redwood can guarantee the reservation and put an autoscale rule exception in place.

If there are alternatives (e.g., 32 guaranteed + 8 burst) that materially reduce cost while meeting latency, we can consider, but need explicit tradeoffs.

Samantha Ho
Head of Infrastructure
Acme AI
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, dev.patel@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 18:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Q2 Dedicated GPU reservation & autoscale exception

Thanks for the heads up. Quick take from infra:

Feasibility: we can reserve capacity in the Dedicated pool and mark the reservation as "pinned" to avoid standard eviction in normal autoscale windows, but there are caveats:
- Physical constraints: current available free A100-equivalent inventory is 44 units for the us-west pool (see attached CSV). Reserving 40 would leave very little headroom for other incoming requests.
- Autoscale rules: exception is possible but must be narrowly scoped. We can implement an exception that prevents reclaiming those machines for general-purpose autoscaling, but we need an approval ticket (EX-4821) for the change and will want rollback windows/monitoring.
- Alternative: suggest guaranteeing 32 GPUs pinned + 8 on burst-with-priority (lower eviction risk) to reduce overall impact.

Technical asks:
1) Exact GPU class (A100-40GB?) — impacts packing and kernel selection.
2) Expected sustained QPS / average sequence length / KV cache expectations — telemetry needed to size.

I can draft the infra change request and propose monitoring hooks (token-level latency, eviction alerts) if Product Ops signs off.

Rishi
Head of Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, Samantha Ho <samantha.ho@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Q2 Dedicated GPU reservation & autoscale exception

Looping the customer back with a proposed pragmatic path. If we offer 32 guaranteed + 8 priority-burst, Acme can adjust their risk profile and save ~15% on committed spend. Proposed plan:
- Week 0 (2026-03-08): sign SOW for 3 months for 32 pinned GPUs + 8 burst-priority units.
- Week 1 (2026-03-15): infra implements exception ticket EX-4821 scoped to the Acme reservation only and deploys monitoring playbook.
- Week 2 (2026-03-22): dry-run in staging with customer traffic (canary) to validate latency.
- Go-live 2026-04-01.

Customer feedback: Samantha — will your SREs accept 32 pinned + 8 burst for the initial window if we commit to the monitoring and an SLA remediation clause?

Dev
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, Samantha Ho <samantha.ho@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Q2 Dedicated GPU reservation & autoscale exception

Agree with Dev's pragmatic approach. Product Ops will approve a scoped autoscale exception under the following conditions:
- Scope: exception applies only to the Acme reservation ID once SOW signed (no global policy changes).
- Size: approve 32 pinned GPUs + 8 priority burst for Apr 1—Jun 30. If metrics show consistent underutilization we will revisit and downscale to avoid wasted capacity.
- Observability: infra must expose token-level latency, per-instance GPU utilization, and eviction alerts to the customer and our Console with 15-minute resolution.
- Fallback: we require an automatic fallback policy that routes traffic to a compatible model variant (quantized) if latency or error rate exceeds threshold for 10 consecutive minutes.

I will file the exception ticket EX-4821 and attach the monitoring checklist. This approval is contingent on a signed SOW and a PO; procurement and finance need to confirm payment terms.

Stephanie
Product Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, dev.patel@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, Samantha Ho <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Q2 Dedicated GPU reservation & autoscale exception

All — procurement side here. We can proceed once we have the following items:
- Signed SOW (please send draft SOW to procurement@acme.ai and cc me) — we have "reserved_capacity_sow_draft.docx" as a starting point.
- Finalized quantity: confirm 32 pinned + 8 burst-priority (we will not lock 40 until we validate utilization in the canary).
- PO with billing contact and payment terms (Net30/Net45).
- Deal ID for finance (we'll use DEAL-2026-ACME-321).

Action items:
- Marissa/Dev: update the SOW to reflect the 32+8 plan and send to Acme procurement.
- Rishi/Stephanie: kick off EX-4821 and attach monitoring checklist.
- Laura: I will open the billing account once SOW and PO are received.

If Acme signs quickly we can file the reservation and mark the capacity as pending hold.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Finance & Procurement
Redwood Inference
